name: CC1312R1F3RGZR
title: SimpleLink Sub-1 GHz wireless MCU, Arm Cortex-M4F, 352 KB flash
summary: A Sub-1 GHz radio system-on-chip: a 48 MHz Arm Cortex-M4F application processor with 352 KB flash, 80 KB parity-checked SRAM and an 8 KB cache, a separate Cortex-M0 radio controller running a software-defined transceiver for bands from 143 MHz to 1315 MHz, and an autonomous ultra-low-power sensor controller with its own 4 KB SRAM, ADC, comparators and timers. It transmits up to +14 dBm (boost mode), receives down to -121 dBm in long-range mode, and idles at 0.85 µA in standby with RTC and full RAM retention. It runs from 1.8 V to 3.8 V with an on-chip buck converter and comes in a 7 mm × 7 mm VQFN48 with 30 GPIOs.
key_figures: 352 KB flash, 256 KB ROM, 80 KB SRAM, 8 KB cache SRAM, 4 KB sensor-controller SRAM
1.8 V to 3.8 V (2.1 V minimum in boost mode)
-121 dBm (SimpleLink long range 2.5 kbps), -110 dBm (50 kbps)

pins.name: RF_N

pins.name: X32K_Q1
pins.function: 32.768 kHz crystal, first terminal. Unused: leave open (or ground).

pins.name: X32K_Q2
pins.function: 32.768 kHz crystal, second terminal. Unused: leave open (or ground).

pins.name: VDDS2
pins.function: 1.8 V to 3.8 V supply for the DIOs; same potential as VDDS.

pins.name: VDDS3
pins.function: 1.8 V to 3.8 V supply for the DIOs; same potential as VDDS.

pins.name: DCOUPL
pins.function: Decoupling node for the internal 1.27 V digital regulator; feeds no outside load.

pins.name: DIO_16
pins.function: General-purpose I/O, also JTAG TDO in 4-pin JTAG; high drive.

pins.name: DIO_17
pins.function: General-purpose I/O, also JTAG TDI in 4-pin JTAG; high drive.

pins.name: DCDC_SW
pins.function: Switch node of the internal buck DC/DC converter; the converter's inductor connects between this pin and VDDR. Unused: leave open.

pins.name: VDDS_DCDC
pins.function: 1.8 V to 3.8 V input of the DC/DC converter; tie to VDDS, also when the converter is unused.

pins.name: VDDR
pins.function: Internal 1.68 V supply rail, fed by the DC/DC converter or, without it, by the main LDO; feeds no outside load.

pins.name: X48M_P
pins.function: 48 MHz crystal, second terminal; a TCXO drives this pin.

pins.name: VDDR_RF
pins.function: Internal 1.68 V supply for the RF section, from the DC/DC converter or LDO; joined to VDDR if the DC/DC converter is left out; feeds no outside load.

pins.name: EGP
pins.function: Exposed pad: the device's only ground; it needs a solid solder joint to board ground.

operation.text: The application and upper protocol layers run on an Arm Cortex-M4F (ARMv7-M, Thumb-2) at 48 MHz, 1.25 DMIPS/MHz, with a single-precision IEEE 754 FPU, single-cycle multiply, hardware divide, saturating arithmetic and a memory protection unit. Debug hardware includes DWT, FPB, ITM and a TPIU with SWO trace. An 8 KB 4-way cache with random replacement sits in front of flash.

A Cortex-M0 inside the RF core drives the analog radio and baseband, builds packets and handles protocol timing on its own; it is reached only through the TI RF driver's command interface and cannot be programmed by the user. Radio formats live in ROM or come as firmware patches in the SDK, so PHY support can be updated in the field (OTA). The RF core can also drive signals for outside RF switches or range extenders. Not every mix of frequency, rate and modulation is supported; SmartRF Studio lists the supported formats and settings.

Four families of formats ship in ROM: the main 2-(G)FSK mode (20 to 1000 kbps), high data rates (up to 2 Msps, 2- or 4-(G)FSK), low data rates (up to 100 ksps, receive bandwidth down to 4 kHz) and SimpleLink Long Range (up to 20 ksps with FEC and DSSS of 1:2, 1:4 or 1:8). Supported protocols include IEEE 802.15.4g, 6LoWPAN, MIOTY, Wireless M-Bus, Wi-SUN, KNX RF, Amazon Sidewalk and the TI 15.4 stack.

Flash is up to 352 KB in 8 KB sectors, programmable in system. Its last sector holds the Customer Configuration area (CCFG), read by the boot ROM and drivers and generated from ccfg.c. System SRAM is up to five 16 KB blocks with parity, usable for data or code, kept in standby by default and cleared to zero at boot. The 8 KB cache is on by default and can be switched to general RAM in CCFG. The 4 KB sensor-controller SRAM is also visible to the main CPU and is not cleared between resets. The 256 KB ROM holds a TI-RTOS kernel, low-level drivers, parts of the radio stacks and a SPI/UART serial bootloader for first programming.

A power-optimized proprietary CPU, programmed in a C-like language with Sensor Controller Studio, runs in standby and active modes and drives its own peripherals without waking the main CPU: the low-power clocked comparator (can wake the system and trigger the ADC, with a reference DAC), capacitive sensing through a constant current source, time-to-digital converter and continuous-time comparator, the 12-bit 200 ksps ADC with eight inputs, analog connection to up to eight GPIOs, and a dedicated SPI master up to 6 MHz. It has a 40-bit accumulator and a 2 MHz low-power mode. Typical jobs are analog and digital sensor reading (UART and I2C bit-banged), pulse counting, waveform generation and key scanning. The main CPU can drive these peripherals too.

Hardware blocks: a TRNG built from 24 ring oscillators, SHA-2 (SHA224, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512), AES with 128- and 256-bit keys, and a public key accelerator handling elliptic-curve math to 512 bits and RSA key-pair generation to 1024 bits. With TI drivers these give ECDH/ECDHE, ECJ-PAKE, ECDSA, NIST P-224/256/384/521, Brainpool 256R1/384R1/512R1, secp256r1, Curve25519 multiplication, HMAC with SHA-2 and AES CCM, GCM, ECB, CBC and CBC-MAC. RSA encryption and Edwards curves can be built on the accelerators but are outside the SDK.

RTC: 70-bit, three channels, clocked by SCLK_LF, running in every mode except shutdown, adjustable for RCOSC_LF drift or a non-32.768 kHz clock, halted by default when a debugger halts the CPU; TI-RTOS uses it as its time base. Four GPTIMERs work as 4 × 32-bit or 8 × 16-bit at up to 48 MHz with one-shot, periodic, PWM, edge-time and edge-count modes, in active and idle. The sensor controller has AUX timers 0 and 1 (16-bit, 2^N prescaler) and AUX timer 2 (16-bit, 24 MHz, 2 MHz or 32 kHz, four capture/compare channels, PWM). The radio has a multichannel 32-bit 4 MHz timer kept in step with the RTC; it is meant for use with the 48 MHz crystal as SCLK_HF. The watchdog runs at 1.5 MHz, cannot be stopped once started, and pauses in standby and under debugger halt.

Two SSIs (SPI, MICROWIRE, TI formats) work as master or slave up to 4 MHz with selectable phase and polarity. Two UARTs reach 3 Mbps. I2S carries digital audio and PDM microphones. I2C runs at 100 kHz and 400 kHz as master or slave. Any digital peripheral can be routed to any DIO through the I/O controller. Every DIO can interrupt and wake the device, has programmable pull-up and pull-down, edge selection, and push-pull or open-drain output.
High-drive pins: 10 (DIO_5), 11 (DIO_6), 12 (DIO_7), 24 (JTAG_TMSC), 26 (DIO_16) and 27 (DIO_17). Analog-capable pins: 36 to 43 (DIO_23 to DIO_30).

On-chip temperature and supply voltage are measured continuously; window comparators interrupt the CPU when either leaves a set window, and the same events can wake the device from standby through the always-on event fabric.

Up to 32 channels move data between any pairing of memory and peripherals (either as source or destination), in 8-, 16- or 32-bit units, with a ping-pong mode for continuous streams; each on-chip module has dedicated channels.
Debug is through cJTAG (IEEE 1149.7) on TMSC and TCKC, the default at boot, or 4-pin JTAG (IEEE 1149.1) after reconfiguration, with TDO on DIO_16 and TDI on DIO_17.

Active runs code with any enabled peripherals. Idle stops the CPU and memory clocks while peripherals keep running; any interrupt returns to active. Standby keeps only the always-on domain; an external pin, RTC or sensor-controller event wakes it, retained peripherals need no setup again, execution resumes in place, and GPIOs are latched. Shutdown turns everything off including the always-on domain and sensor controller; I/Os stay latched, a level change on a pin set as a wake source resets the device, and the reset status register tells this apart from a pin or power-on reset. Only latched I/O states and flash contents survive shutdown. TI drivers in the SDK handle power, RF and clock configuration, and their use is strongly advised.

SCLK_HF (48 MHz) clocks the CPU and peripherals from the internal RCOSC_HF or a 48 MHz crystal; the radio needs a 48 MHz crystal or TCXO. SCLK_MF (2 MHz) always comes from RCOSC_MF and serves the sensor controller's low-power mode and power management. SCLK_LF (32.768 kHz) serves the RTC, the sensor controller and radio-timer resynchronisation around standby; its source is RCOSC_LF (32.8 kHz), a 32.768 kHz crystal or a clock on any DIO. With the crystal or RC source, SCLK_LF can be output to other chips.

A TCXO with clipped-sine output connects to X48M_P through a series capacitor; one with CMOS output connects directly. Probing or stopping the 48 MHz crystal or TCXO while the DC/DC converter runs can permanently damage the device. The 48 MHz crystal load capacitance is adjusted on chip through CCFG, but some frequency, data-rate and modulation combinations need external load capacitors to meet regulations (device errata).

VDDS, VDDS2, VDDS3 and VDDS_DCDC all take 1.8 V to 3.8 V at the same potential. VDDR and VDDR_RF are internal rails trimmed to 1.68 V, fed by the buck converter (inductor from DCDC_SW to VDDR) or by the internal LDO, and must not supply outside circuits. Without the converter, DCDC_SW is left open, VDDS_DCDC goes to VDDS, VDDR_RF stays connected to VDDR, and the 22 µF capacitor stays on VDDR. DCOUPL decouples the internal 1.27 V digital regulator. Boost mode raises VDDR to 1.95 V for +14 dBm output, needs VDDS of at least 2.1 V, and adds about 15 % to system current; the BOD limits are then trimmed to about 2.0 V.

RESET_N has no internal pull-up and needs at least 1 µs low. Wake from reset or shutdown takes 850 µs to 3000 µs depending on charge remaining on the VDDR capacitor; standby to active takes 160 µs. Supply slew must stay within 100 mV/µs rising and 20 mV/µs falling; with a coin cell whose end-of-life resistance is high, a 22 µF VDDS capacitor keeps the falling rate within limit.
The exposed pad is the only ground connection; it is soldered to board ground, which also carries heat away and holds the package mechanically.
The device can run both stack and application (system-on-chip), or run only the wireless stack as a network processor for a host MCU connected over SPI or UART.

TI asks that its reference designs be followed closely, with care over the RF parts, decoupling capacitors, DC/DC converter parts and their grounds. The CC1312REM-XD7793 is the characterization board behind the performance figures; LAUNCHXL-CC1312R1 and LAUNCHXL-CC1352P-4 (up to 13 dBm at 433 MHz) are further references. Integrated matched filter-balun parts can be used on the low-power RF outputs.
